**Subject: Tuesday reading club – an update before the review**

Dear Niamh,

I wanted to send you an update on the Tuesday reading club before the review meeting on Wednesday 18 November. I was sorry to hear in your email of 30 October that it was to be paused from January because of low attendance and the rise in hall insurance costs. I understand there are costs to consider, but the numbers have picked up since then, and I’d be delighted if you could take another look at the decision.

We’ve been meeting upstairs in the meeting room at Knocknacarra library on Tuesdays, from 3.30 to 4.45, since September 2025. We had five children most weeks in September, nine by mid-October, and 14 last Tuesday, 3 November. It’s lovely to see the room filling up, and it would be a terrible pity to pause now, just as the club has taken off.

There are some lovely things happening beyond the numbers, too. Two sisters from a Ukrainian family joined us in October, and the older one now reads to the younger one in English at the end of each session. One boy who wouldn’t open a book in September asked last week if he could take two home. Those are the moments that make the afternoons worthwhile.

We’ve also had a very generous donation from Declan Moran at Salthill Book Nook: 120 books, mostly for the six-to-nine age group, with a good few as Gaeilge. They’ve given the children plenty to choose from.

There’s one other matter I need to tell you about. I met Orla Keane from the Corrib Courier at the farmers’ market, and I got carried away telling her about the club. I said she could “come along any Tuesday”. She’d like to visit with a photographer on Tuesday 24 November.

I was wrong not to check with you first, plain and simple. I know that photographs of the children need your sign-off and parental consent forms. The coverage could be wonderful for the club, but only if it’s done properly. I’m happy to ring Orla and put the visit on hold until you’ve decided. If you do say yes, I can collect the consent forms myself.

I wanted you to have the new attendance figures before the meeting, and I hope you might reconsider the January pause in light of them. I’d be glad to talk through any of this with you beforehand.

With best wishes,  
[Your name]
